text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired for private-vpc-controlplane - customer 'acme-data' - controlplane heartbeats missing from onprem-agent 'acme-agent-17' in us-west-2.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: INC1234567 - private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat (fired)

raj (on-call): acked. I'm on it. Starting root-level checks.

elena (infra): thanks. tagging @maria for customer outreach once we have a short mitigation.

raj (on-call): quick checks - control plane metrics show surge of 401s from agent id acme-agent-17 around 2026-03-15T09:12Z. I can't see heartbeats in the last 2m. Trying to ssh to customer's agent host...

raj (on-call): ssh output and agent logs:
```
$ ssh ec2-user@10.10.200.17
$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50
Mar 15 09:11:58 acme-agent redwood-agent[2345]: time="2026-03-15T09:11:58Z" level=error msg="tls handshake failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid"
Mar 15 09:12:01 acme-agent redwood-agent[2345]: time="2026-03-15T09:12:01Z" level=warn msg="auth failed: server rejected client cert"
```

raj (on-call): looks like TLS validation error on the agent.

elena (infra): control plane rotated leaf certificates during the 03:00 UTC maintenance window (we pushed new CA chain). Most agents should have picked it up automatically. Could be clock skew or agent hasn't pulled new certs.

raj (on-call): checking host clock:
```
$ date -u
Sun Mar 15 09:05:12 UTC 2026
$ curl --head https://controlplane.private.redwood.internal
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

raj (on-call): host clock is ~7 minutes behind. x509 validation is strict; if the agent's time is outside cert validity window it fails.

maria (support): opening support ticket to notify customer (ACME) and ask them to confirm NTP for their onprem host. Ticket #ACME-7821. I'll post a short note in the ticket summarizing the steps.

raj (on-call): performing quick mitigation: enable NTP and restart agent.
```
sudo timedatectl set-ntp true
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 50 --no-pager
```

raj (on-call): after restart logs:
```
Mar 15 09:13:08 acme-agent redwood-agent[2401]: time="2026-03-15T09:13:08Z" level=info msg="successfully authenticated to control plane, heartbeat streaming enabled"
```

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded for INC1234567 by raj (on-call).

elena (infra): good find. Can you confirm heartbeats are stable for 5m and then we'll close? Also add a follow-up for detection.

raj (on-call): heartbeats resumed at 09:13:08 UTC. Monitoring for 5m window.

kim (eng-manager): action items: 1) add clock-skew check to agent healthcheck (alerts when >2m), 2) augment runbook to include `timedatectl` step, 3) follow up with security about cert rotation visibility to agents. Assigning to @raj and @elena.

maria (support): customer notified in ACME ticket: "We observed an agent clock skew on your device which prevented TLS validation after our cert rotation. We applied NTP and restarted the agent; it reconnected. Please confirm NTP is allowed from your network and consider adding a local NTP server."

raj (on-call): Confirming 7m of stable heartbeats since reconnect; no further 401s in logs.

incident-bot: Incident INC1234567 - private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat - resolved by raj (on-call). Duration: 00:04:12. Severity: P2. Root cause: on-prem agent clock skew causing TLS validation failures against newly rotated control plane certs. Mitigation: enabled NTP and restarted agent. Follow-ups: agent healthcheck alert for clock skew, update runbook, customer outreach queued (ACME-7821).

kim (eng-manager): thanks team. I'll schedule a quick retro item on Monday to tighten rotation docs.

maria (support): closing customer loop once we get confirmation from ACME. I'll paste this thread into the ticket.

raj (on-call): marking notes in incident tracker and will add log snippets.

elena (infra): noting we should test cert rotation on a staging agent with induced clock skew to avoid surprises.

incident-bot: Incident closed. If recurrence detected, PagerDuty will re-open.
